reason: The text describes a hierarchical structure of leadership and resource distribution rather than collaboration. Pharaoh appoints Joseph to sole authority over Egypt (41:39-44), and when famine comes, Pharaoh directs the people to go to Joseph and obey his instructions (41:55). Joseph, as the appointed leader, distributes grain from the stored supplies to the Egyptian people. The people are recipients of Joseph's administration and stewardship during the famine, not collaborators in governance or shared work. The relationship depicted is one of top-down leadership and obedience, not mutual collaboration where leaders and people work together as partners.
